correctness.rationale: Normalized angular monomials diagonalize the radial indicator, and squared radius t has Gamma(n+1,1) density at degree n. Integrating the derivative of t^(n+1)e^(−t) gives (n+1)!(λ_(n+1)−λ_n)=F(n). Also λ_(n+1)≤b_m λ_n/(n+1) gives eventual strict decay to zero. For an exponential sum with r distinct exponents and nonzero coefficients, divide by the first exponential and differentiate, leaving r−1 terms; Rolle with multiplicities inductively gives at most r−1 real zeros counted with multiplicity. This verifies the required bound directly because the endpoint terms all alternate and there are 2m terms, or 2m−1 when the zero endpoint is omitted. For k local-maximum plateaux not beginning at zero, there are at least 2k−1 strict reversals in the nonzero first differences: one inside each pair of entrance and exit signs, and one between plateaux. If the first plateau begins at zero, there are at least 2k−2; both bounds imply k≤m using distinct roots between samples with opposing signs. This handles ties without an extrapolated starting sign. At a global maximizing index n>0, F(n−1)≥0≥F(n); a zero in [n−1,n] always places n in the specified floor-and-successor set, including when the zero is an integer. Positivity and decay ensure a maximum exists. For sharpness take intervals [jL,jL+1]. At n=jL−2 and jL+2 the new-to-old endpoint ratio on interval j has logarithm −3/(2jL)+O(L⁻²) and 5/(2jL)+O(L⁻²), respectively. After dividing by (n+1)!, the main signed contribution has magnitude comparable to L^(−3/2) by Stirling; each other ring is exponentially small by k−j−j log(k/j)>0. Hence there is a local maximum in each disjoint peak window for L large at fixed m.
residual_risks: The numerical file tests strict peaks and finite samples; the proof supplies the plateau cases and universal claims. Candidate cardinality is not a bound on the cost of finding or certifying real roots.

The pass concerns that supported theorem as a whole, not priority for the classical tool, the single-ring case or the overlapping claims in other records.

value.rationale: The theorem bounds the number of high-concentration degree bands by the number of radial components, with equality possible for all m. The exact finite candidate set eliminates dependence of the count of spectral evaluations on large endpoint radii and covers ties and disk components. This addresses arbitrary separated radial masks, not only particular numerical examples or a norm envelope, while making no claim of bounded computational effort for isolating the roots.
residual_risks: The result is radial, finite-component, one-complex-dimensional and Gaussian; no conclusion about signed or nonradial masks.
